Subject: Azure Marketplace private offer — draft term sheet and next steps

Hi Elena / Marketplace team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, attached is our proposed term sheet for the Azure private offer and a pricing workbook with the dedicated SKU and burst capacity options. Key items we'd like to align on before you publish the private offer on the Contoso tenant:

- Purchase order flow & invoice cadence (Net 30 vs Net 45)
- Liability & indemnity caps (Contoso suggested language is in your PO terms)
- Data residency / deployment model (hosted private vs VPC/private deploy)
- SLA uptime & remedies for enterprise dedicated capacity

Can you confirm who on your procurement/legal team will own redlines? If convenient, propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the biggest items — we'll bring legal and our Partnerships lead.

Attachments:
- redwood-marketplace-term-sheet-v1.pdf (term sheet, SOW-level items)
- redwood-azure-private-plan-pricing.xlsx (pricing by capacity tier)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly — thanks for the materials. I shared the term sheet with our procurement and legal teams; initial comments attached (we used our standard PO terms template to highlight the areas that will require negotiation).

High-level items from our side:
- We need a clear indemnity and insurance paragraph; Contoso cannot accept open-ended indemnities and asks for a 3x revenue cap or $5M (whichever is lower).
- Data residency: Contoso prefers that customer data for PHI-adjacent workloads be hosted in our VNet (Azure Private Link). If Redwood requires hosted-only, we need an explicit exception and SOC2 + encryption attestations.
- Payment terms: procurement prefers Net 45 for new vendors; we can escalate Net 30 for strategic partners but need approval.
- Change control & release windows: Contoso requires 30 days notice for breaking changes to runtime behavior used in production.

I've attached "Contoso-PO-terms.docx" with inline comments. Procurement suggests a 60-day review window, but we can accelerate if both legal teams are responsive.

If helpful, let's do a 30-45 minute joint session Thursday 11/6 at 10am PT with legal on the line.

Regards,
Elena Rossi
VP, Strategic Sourcing
Contoso Health

Attachments:
- Contoso-PO-terms.docx (redlines)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@contoso-health.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>

Elena — really appreciate the quick turnaround and the detailed redlines. A few quick notes from Partnerships:

- Liability cap: we generally accept limiting to contract value, but the $5M floor on the Contoso side is higher than typical for the early stage of this commercial relationship. Can we propose a 12-month revenue cap (or $2M) and a step-up approach tied to committed capacity?
- Data residency: Redwood supports VNet/private deployments via our Private offering, but that typically requires an onboarding SOW and infrastructure costs. We'd prefer to avoid making VNet mandatory for the initial private offer — can Contoso accept the hosted private option with SOC2 + customer-managed encryption keys?
- Payment terms: we're flexible, Net 45 is acceptable for enterprise pilots, but we would like Net 30 for production commitments.

Looping in Jordan from Legal to provide counterlanguage on the liability and indemnity items. Stephanie — can you confirm whether the pricing workbook already includes the one‑time onboarding fees for VPC options?

Thanks — happy to take the Thursday slot if that works for Contoso.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@contoso-health.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Microsoft Marketplace PM <mpm-marketplace@microsoft.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 09:04:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace private offer — draft term sheet and next steps

Elena / team — thanks for the redlines. I reviewed Contoso's PO template and our counter proposal is attached (RDW-Counter-terms-v2.pdf) with tracked changes. Summary of recommended positions:

- Liability: limit Redwood's total liability to fees paid under the order in the prior 12 months, except for gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- Indemnity: mutual indemnities with third-party IP carve-outs; exclude consequential damages and lost profit claims.
- Data residency: we can commit to SOC2 Type II and customer-managed keys; requiring a VNet-hosted deployment is a material change — if Contoso insists, we'll scope that as a separate SOW with estimated onboarding costs.
- Payment terms: willing to accept Net 45 for the initial 6-month pilot; Net 30 thereafter for committed capacity.

If these points are acceptable, we'll prepare a countersigned DocuSign package and ask Microsoft to publish the private offer once both parties execute. Jordan (legal) is available for the Thursday 11/6 10am PT call.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- RDW-Counter-terms-v2.pdf (redlines)

Jordan / Kimberly / Aditya — thank you. The counterproposal looks reasonable; Procurement will accept the liability language tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months and the mutual indemnity carve-outs. Contoso is willing to accept hosted private with SOC2 + CMK for the pilot; if after pilot we require VNet-hosted deployment, we'll open a separate procurement SOW.

Action items:
- Contoso will upload the signed PO once DocuSign arrives.
- Contoso requests Marketplace PM to publish the private offer after both signatures (please advise expected lead time).
- We'll confirm the start date for the pilot in the PO (aiming for 11/20 start).
